additional_info.subject: RE: ID0403090-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S5 170003620] Charger delivers less power CRM:00643001242
additional_info.body:
Hi
Johannes,
We have analysed the complete logs and the below are the analysis.
The logs snapshot that I’ve shared below demonstrate that the EV functions as the Master & charger functions as Slave. The charger provided the current and voltage that the EV demanded. As you can see from the multiple instances, the EV’s target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to certain SOC using CC, and then it switches to CV mode gradually based on EV requirements. During this phase, the EV's target current drops to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing.
As you can see the highlighted ones as the EV changes its current, the charger automatically adjusted the current and in the second snapshot you can see the EV demands around 300A and yet again over delivers it.
Based on this analysis, we conclude that there is no issue with the EVSE. I hope this addresses your concerns. If there are no further questions, shall we proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

I'm not saying that the truck is the problem. What I meant to say is that the charger is delivering power as the EV demands, and the logs show no indication that the EV is requesting more power than the charger is providing. Regarding the power converter schema in the charger logs, this is an additional log introduced in the latest firmware version that our charger is running. You can see that the PLC error flag is not true, it is simply set from False to False.

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: AW: ID0403090-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S5 170003620] Charger delivers less power CRM:00643001242
additional_info.body:
Hi
Johannes,
Thanks for the update. Regarding your query, if you review the logs again, you'll notice a parameter called EVSE_DESpwr, which indicates the allotment power to that outlet. As per the logs, it shows around 373kW, while our charger is rated for 400kW. The power will only increase if the EV demands more current, which is why we're seeing only 373kW of power. If any power module had failed, it would be reflected in the EVSE_DESpwr parameter with reduced power and would result in a power converter error in SCB as well as in the charger logs. Additionally, the power converter F:1 indicates that a fast shutdown was performed successfully, and the "Module PowerOff DueTo Fault" error you mentioned appears in the error flags of the power converter after the 'F' state, with either E01 or EXX.
I hope this answers your query. If there are no further questions, may I proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
